slice: Sole RegExp literal programs evaluate without native compilation

coordinatorRequirements.1-shape: soleRegExpLiteral() inspects the parsed Module: exactly one statement, kind 'expression', expression kind 'regexp'. Comments, whitespace and a trailing semicolon are absorbed by the parser; anything else (two statements, parenthesized, member access, declarations, empty program) takes the compiled path. No string matching.
coordinatorRequirements.2-early-errors: Both paths parse with the same parser call before the fast-path check; parseRegExp (the RegExp early-error validator) rejects invalid patterns/flags as SyntaxError in direct sloppy/strict and indirect eval (differential corpus: /(/, /a/gg, /a/x, /a/uv, /[b-a]/, /\u{110000}/u, duplicate groups, /\p{Foo}/u, line terminator in body).
coordinatorRequirements.3-fresh-object: createRegExpLiteral(pattern, flags, context.realm, context.global.hooks) per evaluation, the same call, realm and hooks that the compiled entry emits ($errors = $script.realm, $global.hooks). Tests assert distinct identity, lastIndex 0, RegExp.prototype, own keys and flag getters.
coordinatorRequirements.4-no-environment-effects: The shape has no declarations; the compiled entry's declaration plan is empty. Unit tests assert unchanged global keys and lexical bindings and an unchanged active context; the differential asserts no new global properties.
coordinatorRequirements.5-differential: packages/js-engine/test/regexp-literal-eval-differential.test.ts: 36 sources × (direct sloppy, direct strict, indirect) in the lowered Node realm, fast path vs compiled path (source + empty block), with identical printed results and compile counts proving which path ran (fast 0, compiled 6). A flags mutation of the fast path fails 10 cases.

note: The general eval preparation cost remains P's; this path is complementary and covers only sole RegExp literal programs.
